It is loud, it smells of exhaust, the queue is exposed to the sun, and the ride itself takes five minutes at a crawl. On any objective measure it is the weakest major attraction at Magic Kingdom and it consistently posts waits of forty minutes or more.

It stays because of one thing. At 32 inches a child can ride with an adult, and at 54 inches they can drive alone — and for a certain kind of seven-year-old, holding a real steering wheel and pressing a real accelerator is the highlight of the entire trip. If that describes a child in your party, the wait is worth it. If not, this is the easiest skip in the park.
experience: The queue runs alongside the track under partial cover, and it is loud enough that conversation is difficult. In summer this is one of the worst waits at Magic Kingdom — hot, noisy, and the exhaust smell carries.

Cars are two-seaters with a bench, a steering wheel, and a floor accelerator. An adult riding with a small child typically operates the pedal while the child steers, because the pedal requires steady pressure for five minutes and a child's leg will not hold it. Children driving alone must be 54 inches.

The lap is a five-minute crawl around a landscaped track with a guide rail keeping you roughly in lane. Steering does something — you bounce off the rail if you oversteer — but you cannot leave the lane. The car behind you will hit you at least twice; this is normal and unavoidable, and it is the part small kids find most exciting.
tips: Ride it in the first hour or skip it. A forty-five-minute midday wait for five minutes of exhaust fumes at seven miles per hour is the worst trade at Magic Kingdom, and the queue offers no shade worth the name.
The adult should work the pedal and let the child steer. A five-year-old cannot hold the accelerator down for a full lap, and the ride stopping halfway through is the standard rookie outcome.
54 inches to drive alone is the number that matters to older kids, and it is one of the few requirements at Disney where the taller child gets the better experience rather than just access.
Rider Switch is available, which is worth knowing because plenty of parents assume a 32-inch ride does not need it.

If your child is under 54 inches and desperate to drive solo, the honest answer is that no other attraction on Walt Disney World property offers it. Manage expectations before you queue rather than at the loading gate.
attractions.bestTime: The first hour after opening; the queue is unbearable in midday summer heat.
attractions.typicalWait: 30 to 60 minutes for most of the day, which is out of proportion to what it delivers.

faqs.q: What is the height requirement for Tomorrowland Speedway?
faqs.a: 32 inches to ride with an adult, and 54 inches to drive alone. That 54-inch mark is one of the highest solo requirements at Walt Disney World and is the number most families are actually asking about.

faqs.q: Can kids really drive the cars at Tomorrowland Speedway?
faqs.a: They steer, within limits. A steel guide rail runs down the center of each lane, so the car cannot leave the track no matter what the driver does. Steering input moves the car within the lane and produces a bump off the rail if you oversteer, which most children find satisfying.

faqs.q: Is Tomorrowland Speedway worth the wait?
faqs.a: Honestly, only if you have a child who specifically wants to drive. It is loud, it smells of exhaust, the queue has almost no shade, and the ride is a five-minute crawl. For that one child it can be the best thing they do all trip; for everyone else it is the clearest skip at Magic Kingdom.

faqs.q: How fast do the cars go on Tomorrowland Speedway?
faqs.a: About seven miles per hour at full throttle. The perception of speed is much higher for a child holding the wheel, which is the entire point of the attraction.

attractions.name: Monsters, Inc. Laugh Floor

scary.notes: Nothing frightening. The only discomfort is social: the animated characters pick audience members out of the crowd and put their face on screen, which some shy adults and teenagers find genuinely mortifying.

accessibility.notes: Level theater with wheelchair positions and no transfer required. Captioning is displayed on the screens themselves. The show relies heavily on spoken comedy, so assistive listening devices are worth collecting from Guest Relations for guests with hearing loss.

attractions.summary: A live improv comedy show performed by animated monsters who talk directly to the audience.
description: An animated monster hosts a stand-up set on screens at the front of a theater, and the whole thing is live — a puppeteer and voice performer behind the scenes sees the audience and responds in real time. Characters pick people out of the crowd, comment on their shirts, put their face on the big screen and improvise around them.

The technology behind it is more interesting than the jokes: a real-time animation system that lets a performer drive a rendered character conversationally. When it works, it produces genuinely surprising moments. When the operator is having an off day, it is fifteen minutes of dad jokes.

You can text a joke to the show before it starts using the number posted in the pre-show, and jokes chosen from that queue get read out. Almost nobody does it, which means the odds of yours being picked are much better than you would expect.
tips: Text a joke to the number displayed in the pre-show area. Very few guests bother, so a decent short joke has a real chance of being read to the theater.
Sit in the middle rows if you want to be picked on and at the very back if you do not. The characters can see the audience and they target people who look approachable.
Wear something with a slogan or an unusual hat if you want to be part of the show. The performers work from what they can see.

It is fifteen minutes of air conditioning with a wait that is essentially the next show cycle, and it is directly across from Buzz Lightyear — a good pairing for a mid-afternoon indoor block in Tomorrowland.
attractions.bestTime: Mid-afternoon; the wait is one show cycle at nearly any hour.
attractions.typicalWait: 10 to 25 minutes, essentially just the next showing.
